title: Formal justifying act is complex — intellect and will informed together
source_text: CXII. Itaque puto formalem & proprium fidei salvificae actum, & ratione cujus justificare dicenda est, generalius concipi & exprimi debere; & ita ut in se includat & involvat plures actus particulares fidem illam constituentes. Quandoquidem, ut jam est a nobis observatum, ex consensu maximae partis Doctorum Scholae Reformatae, fides illa non est unus simplex vel habitus, vel actus, sed complexum plurium actuum, vel habituum, qui non solum intellectum, sed ipsam quoque voluntatem informant.
pass_a_gloss: Therefore I think the formal and proper act of saving faith, and that by reason of which it is to be said to justify, ought to be conceived and expressed more generally; and so that it includes and involves in itself several particular acts that constitute that faith. Since, as we have already observed, by the consent of the greatest part of the Doctors of the Reformed School, that faith is not one simple habit or act, but a complex of several acts or habits which inform not only the intellect but the will itself as well.
pass_b_english: So the formal proper act by which saving faith justifies should be stated more generally — as including several particular acts that constitute that faith.
Most Reformed doctors agree: justifying faith is not one simple habit or act, but a complex of acts/habits informing intellect and will together.
